title: The Last Mixtape
premise: Beatrix Eastwick has spent ten years keeping his head down in the small town of Marrow's Bend, baking his grief and longing into bread for a family that isn't quite his own. When his grandmother dies and leaves him her recipe box, he discovers cards that aren't recipes at all — they're instructions, confessions, and one card addressed to a boy named Theo who vanished from town a decade ago. Following the cards pulls Beatrix into an old promise between three families, a debt of silence his grandmother helped keep, and a friendship with the last person who might know what happened. To honor her, Beatrix must break the loyalty she built her life on and tell the truth — even though it costs him the only family he has left. In the end, the truth doesn't shatter the found family; it remakes it, and Beatrix finally bakes bread with nothing hidden inside.
about_author: Rafael Underhill grew up above his aunt's bakery in coastal Maine, where he learned that kitchens keep secrets better than diaries do. He writes stories about quiet kids who inherit loud truths, and this is his second novel.

chapters.title: Proofing
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Ten years after arriving at the Eastwicks' bakery as a foster kid, Beatrix bakes the morning loaves, careful and invisible, while Grandma June critiques his sourdough and calls him 'the keeper.' Emotional beat: belonging that feels borrowed.

chapters.title: The Card That Isn't Bread
chapters.summary: Grandma June dies peacefully in her sleep. Sorting the recipe box, Beatrix finds a card labeled 'For Bea — when I'm gone' containing directions to a locked cellar hatch, not a dish. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: grief interrupted by vertigo.

chapters.title: Down Where the Flour Kept Cold
chapters.summary: Beatrix opens the cellar hatch and finds a tin box: newspaper clippings about Theo Marsh, a boy who disappeared ten years ago, plus half a mixtape labeled 'T & J.' POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: the past has been living under his feet.

chapters.title: Everyone Remembers Differently
chapters.summary: Beatrix asks Aunt Colleen about Theo; she goes pale and changes the subject, then warns him to leave it. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: first crack in the family's careful silence.

chapters.title: The Boy at the Bus Stop
chapters.summary: New character: Wren Okafor, Theo's younger cousin, back in town clearing out her grandmother's house. She recognizes the mixtape label instantly. POV alternates to Wren. Emotional beat: two lonely people recognize each other.

chapters.title: Side A
chapters.summary: They play the tape; between songs is a recording of teenage June and Theo planning to run away together — and mentioning 'the money in the wall' at the old cannery. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: the dead speaking plainly.

chapters.title: Recipe Card #7
chapters.summary: A second card surfaces: 'Loyalty is a loaf you bake twice. The second time, tell the truth.' Beatrix realizes June left him a trail on purpose. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: being trusted from beyond.

chapters.title: What the Cannery Kept
chapters.summary: Sneaking into the derelict cannery, they find a wall cavity — empty except for a fresh boot print. Someone got there first. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: they are not the only ones looking.

chapters.title: Uncle Dev's New Truck
chapters.summary: Beatrix notices Uncle Dev — June's son — suddenly flush with cash and defensive. He snaps at questions about the cannery. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: suspicion turning toward family.

chapters.title: Wren's House of Boxes
chapters.summary: Wren's chapter: sorting her late grandmother's things, she finds letters proving Theo wrote home after he disappeared — someone intercepted them. Emotional beat: hope with teeth.

chapters.title: The Interception
chapters.summary: The letters were returned by 'June Eastwick,' but the handwriting is wrong. Beatrix confronts the possibility that June protected a lie to protect Dev. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: loyalty vs. truth begins to hurt.

chapters.title: Bread as Confession
chapters.summary: Beatrix bakes June's 'honesty loaf' recipe exactly and leaves a slice on Dev's porch with card #7 tucked under it. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: courage delivered warm.

chapters.title: Dev Breaks
chapters.summary: Dev confesses: as a teen he stole the cannery money, let Theo take the blame, and Theo ran rather than be sent away. June knew and stayed silent to keep her son out of prison. POV shifts to Dev briefly. Emotional beat: shame finally spoken aloud.

chapters.title: Where Theo Went
chapters.summary: Dev reveals the last address he ever had for Theo — a town two states over. Wren wants to go immediately; Beatrix hesitates, terrified of leaving the bakery. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: fear vs. duty.

chapters.title: The Bakery Without Its Keeper
chapters.summary: Colleen discovers the cellar open and the tin gone; she accuses Beatrix of betraying June's memory and threatens to send him away like before. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: the family he chose may disown him for the truth.

chapters.title: Two Tickets and a Loaf
chapters.summary: Beatrix chooses Wren and the truth. They bus out with a cooler of bread to sell along the way, following the address. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: found family forming in motion.

chapters.title: The Man Who Bakes on Tuesdays
chapters.summary: In the far town they find Theo — alive, working a bakery, going by another name. He refuses at first: exposing Dev now would wreck Dev's kids' lives. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: truth has a price even for its victim.

chapters.title: Card #12: The Last Recipe
chapters.summary: Beatrix reads June's final card, mailed ahead years ago to Theo's bakery: her full confession and apology, asking Theo to decide. Theo weeps. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: June's loyalty was love wearing armor.

chapters.title: Climax: The Town Meeting
chapters.summary: Theo returns to Marrow's Bend unannounced during the memorial for June. In front of the whole town, Beatrix stands beside him and tells everything — refusing to let Dev hide or Theo vanish again. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: the truth spoken at maximum cost.

chapters.title: Aftermath, Unsweetened
chapters.summary: Consequences land: Dev turns himself in; Colleen, shattered, tells Beatrix he can stay but not speak to her yet. Wren decides to finish school in Marrow's Bend. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: grief without anesthesia.

chapters.title: Rising
chapters.summary: Weeks later, the bakery reopens under shared stewardship — Beatrix, Colleen thawing, and Theo consulting on weekends. The town slowly forgives what it understands. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: family rebuilt on truth instead of silence.

chapters.title: The First Honest Loaf
chapters.summary: Final scene: Beatrix bakes a new recipe of his own invention, labels the card 'For whoever comes next,' and slides it into June's box. Nothing hidden inside. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: inheritance continued, freely given.
